findings.description: 一喜一憂 is reduced to rejoicing, dropping the alternating delight and concern in the reactions that absorb George’s attention.

contexts.japanese:
文字通りデレデレする僕の眼中に、世界最大の水族館の大水槽はもはや映らない。
紗音が魚たちと戯れて一喜一憂する姿を映し続けるのみだ。
contexts.japanesePC: 紗音が魚たちと戯れて一喜一憂する姿を映し続けるのみだ。
contexts.japanesePS3:
文字通りデレデレする僕の眼中に、世界最大の水族館の大水槽はもはや映らない。
紗音が魚たちと戯れて一喜一憂する姿を映し続けるのみだ。
contexts.WH: Instead, I see Shannon rejoicing and playing with the fish.
contexts.MG:
I'm so entranced that I barely notice that massive tank in the world's largest aquarium anymore.
Instead, all I see are the expressions flitting across Shannon's face as she plays with the fish.
contexts.UP:
I was so entranced that I no longer even noticed the big tank of the world's largest aquarium.
Instead, I saw only Shannon happily playing with the fish, all her changing emotions showing on her face.
contexts.note: MG flitting expressions and UP changing emotions restore variation, but neither explicitly preserves paired delight/concern in 一喜一憂; UP happily retains positive framing. Original WH rejoicing wording is not copied into these witness excerpts.

MG.japanese: 古風な言い方で喩えるなら、これこそまさに薔薇色の日々…。文字通りデレデレする僕の眼中に、世界最大の水族館の大水槽はもはや映らない。紗音が魚たちと戯れて一喜一憂する姿を映し続けるのみだ。
MG.translation: To use an old-fashioned phrase, these really are rose-colored days I'm living in... I'm so entranced that I barely notice that massive tank in the world's largest aquarium anymore. Instead, all I see are the expressions flitting across Shannon's face as she plays with the fish.

UP.japanese: 古風な言い方で喩えるなら、これこそまさに薔薇色の日々…。文字通りデレデレする僕の眼中に、世界最大の水族館の大水槽はもはや映らない。紗音が魚たちと戯れて一喜一憂する姿を映し続けるのみだ。
UP.translation: To use an old‐fashioned phrase, these would be truly rose‐colored days... I was so entranced that I no longer even noticed the big tank of the world's largest aquarium. Instead, I saw only Shannon happily playing with the fish, all her changing emotions showing on her face.

findings.sourceReading: George sees only Shannon as she interacts with the fish and reacts with delight or concern to each little thing.
findings.alternative: The scene already shows her enthusiasm and embarrassment, and this is an affectionate use of a stock idiom rather than proof of deep unhappiness. Still, “rejoicing” makes the observed reactions uniformly positive.

findings.description: 自分ひとりの価値観しか持てない becomes “stick to their own view,” turning an inability to possess more than one’s own perspective into language of adhering to it.

contexts.japanese:
人間というのは、どんなに見聞を広めようとも、所詮は自分ひとりの価値観しか持てない。
だからこそ、異なる価値観を持つ人間と交流することはこんなにも面白いのかもしれない。
contexts.japanesePC: 人間というのは、どんなに見聞を広めようとも、所詮は自分ひとりの価値観しか持てない。だからこそ、異なる価値観を持つ人間と交流することはこんなにも面白いのかもしれない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
人間というのは、どんなに見聞を広めようとも、所詮は自分ひとりの価値観しか持てない。
だからこそ、異なる価値観を持つ人間と交流することはこんなにも面白いのかもしれない。
contexts.WH: No matter how far humans broaden their experiences, they stick to their own view of the world in the end.  Maybe that's why it's so interesting to mingle with people who have a different worldview.
contexts.MG:
No matter how far humans broaden their experiences, they always end up viewing the world through the lense of their own values.
Maybe that's why it's so interesting to interact with people who have different worldviews.
contexts.UP:
No matter how far humans broaden their experiences, in the end, they can only hold a single personal worldview.
Maybe that's why it's so interesting to interact with someone who has a different worldview.
contexts.note: MG viewing through own-values lens preserves single-perspective limitation; UP explicitly only a single personal worldview. Neither says stubbornly stick to views.

MG.japanese: 人間というのは、どんなに見聞を広めようとも、所詮は自分ひとりの価値観しか持てない。だからこそ、異なる価値観を持つ人間と交流することはこんなにも面白いのかもしれない。
MG.translation: No matter how far humans broaden their experiences, they always end up viewing the world through the lense of their own values. Maybe that's why it's so interesting to interact with people who have different worldviews.

UP.japanese: 人間というのは、どんなに見聞を広めようとも、所詮は自分ひとりの価値観しか持てない。だからこそ、異なる価値観を持つ人間と交流することはこんなにも面白いのかもしれない。
UP.translation: No matter how far humans broaden their experiences, in the end, they can only hold a single personal worldview. Maybe that's why it's so interesting to interact with someone who has a different worldview.

findings.sourceReading: However much experience a person gains, they can ultimately possess only their own individual value framework; exchange with someone whose framework differs is therefore interesting.
findings.alternative: “Stick to” may loosely express persistence rather than stubborn refusal, and the next sentence retains the value of different perspectives. The source nonetheless describes a limit of individual subjectivity, not a choice to adhere to beliefs.

MG.translation: Shannon, who spent her days as a servant on a small island 10 kilometers in circumference called Rokkenjima, said that with a smile.

UP.translation: Shannon, who spent her days as a servant on a small island ten kilometers in circumference called Rokkenjima, said that with a smile.

findings.sourceReading: Shannon lives as a servant on the small island Rokkenjima, approximately ten kilometers in overall length.
findings.alternative: Overall length can be a loosely specified dimension, but it does not mean perimeter; no surrounding reference to a circuit supplies circumference. The small-island comparison survives.

findings.description: 白い目で見る becomes staring with “blank eyes,” losing the idiom’s disapproval or contempt.

contexts.japanese:
傍から見ていたなら、僕たちは何と微笑ましく、そして何と恥ずかしい二人なのだろう。
しかし二人になってみて初めてわかる。
僕たちにとってはこのやり取りが全てで、世界なのだ。
だから世界の外側の人がどんなに白い目で見たって、僕たちは気付かない。
……なるほど、カップルがＴＰＯを弁えずにイチャつきたがる心情を、この歳にしてようやく理解する。
contexts.japanesePC: だから世界の外側の人がどんなに白い目で見たって、僕たちは気付かない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
傍から見ていたなら、僕たちは何と微笑ましく、そして何と恥ずかしい二人なのだろう。
しかし二人になってみて初めてわかる。
僕たちにとってはこのやり取りが全てで、世界なのだ。
だから世界の外側の人がどんなに白い目で見たって、僕たちは気付かない。
……なるほど、カップルがＴＰＯを弁えずにイチャつきたがる心情を、この歳にしてようやく理解する。
contexts.WH: That's why no matter how much everyone else stared at us with blank eyes, we wouldn't have noticed it.
contexts.MG:
To anyone watching us, we might seem like an incredibly charming and embarrassing couple.
But it's only after becoming a couple that you realize.
To us, this exchange of words is everything, our entire world.
That's why no matter how much everyone else stares at us with blank expressions, we never notice.
......Indeed, at this age, I finally understand the feelings of couples who want to endlessly flirt without any regard for their surroundings.
contexts.UP:
To anyone watching us, we might have seemed like a pretty humorous—and above all embarrassing—couple.
But it's only after becoming a couple that you realize.
This banter means the world to us, and is our world.
So, no matter how cold the looks we might have been getting from other people, we wouldn't even notice.
......Indeed, at this age, I finally understand the feelings of couples who want to endlessly flirt without any regard to their surroundings.
contexts.note: MG blank expressions loses disapproval; UP cold looks restores it.

MG.japanese:
傍から見ていたなら、僕たちは何と微笑ましく、そして何と恥ずかしい二人なのだろう。しかし二人になってみて初めてわかる。僕たちにとってはこのやり取りが全てで、世界なのだ。
だから世界の外側の人がどんなに白い目で見たって、僕たちは気付かない。
MG.translation: To anyone watching us, we might seem like an incredibly charming and embarrassing couple. But it's only after becoming a couple that you realize. To us, this exchange of words is everything, our entire world. That's why no matter how much everyone else stares at us with blank expressions, we never notice.

UP.japanese:
傍から見ていたなら、僕たちは何と微笑ましく、そして何と恥ずかしい二人なのだろう。しかし二人になってみて初めてわかる。僕たちにとってはこのやり取りが全てで、世界なのだ。
だから世界の外側の人がどんなに白い目で見たって、僕たちは気付かない。
UP.translation:
To anyone watching us, we might have seemed like a pretty humorous—and above all embarrassing—couple. But it's only after becoming a couple that you realize. This banter means the world to us, and is our world.
So, no matter how cold the looks we might have been getting from other people, we wouldn't even notice.

findings.sourceReading: Their flirtatious exchange is their entire world, so they do not notice however disapprovingly people outside that world look at them.
findings.alternative: The following remark about disregard for surroundings still suggests public impropriety. Blank eyes can suggest lack of enthusiasm but do not express the source’s judgment.

彼女を恥ずかしがらせて嫌な思いがさせたいわけじゃない。

findings.sourceReading: George enjoys controlling and monopolizing her emotional reactions, but wants to calibrate the teasing: he does not want to embarrass her and make her feel unpleasant.
findings.alternative: The English still ends the topic and says he wants to treat her lightly. Both can be compatible with caring about her, but the explicit reputational motive is invented and her unpleasant feelings are omitted.

contexts.MG:

findings.description: The wish ご縁があったらな and her admission that she fantasized about it become “When I started this relationship ... it just felt like a delusion.”

contexts.japanese:

findings.sourceReading: Unlike George, Shannon had imagined or fantasized that she might enter a relationship with the considerate, gentlemanly George. She is embarrassed to admit that prior wish.
findings.alternative: The English retains imagination and delusion vocabulary and the compliment, and George’s next reply credits her believing heart. Its final clause nonetheless moves the fantasy from a hoped-for future to her reaction to an actual relationship.

findings.description: The contrast between what she regards as everything and its small share of his total explanation becomes “What she chooses to believe weighs little in my thoughts.”

contexts.japanese:
出会いを、奇跡や偶然で修飾したがるのは紗音に限らず、女の子の普遍的な考え方なんだろうか。
男の僕にとって、女の子との出会いは、気に入られようとする７０％の努力と、２０％の勇気。
そして１０％の偶然。
彼女が全てだと信じるものは、僕の中では全体を占めるウェートが少ない。
…そういう考え方自体が、男性的で打算的なのだろうか。
でも、それを口に出して言えば、どんな魔法も解けてしまう。
僕たちがこういう関係になるまでには、たくさんの偶然や歩み寄り、双方のたくさんの努力があったと思う。
それら全ての積み重ねの上に、今の二人きりの幸せな時間があり、
それを魔法と呼ぶならば、彼女の言い方は決しておかしなものではない。
contexts.japanesePC: 彼女が全てだと信じるものは、僕の中では全体を占めるウェートが少ない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
出会いを、奇跡や偶然で修飾したがるのは紗音に限らず、女の子の普遍的な考え方なんだろうか。
男の僕にとって、女の子との出会いは、気に入られようとする７０％の努力と、２０％の勇気。
そして１０％の偶然。

…そういう考え方自体が、男性的で打算的なのだろうか。

僕たちがこういう関係になるまでには、たくさんの偶然や歩み寄り、双方のたくさんの努力があったと思う。
それら全ての積み重ねの上に、今の二人きりの幸せな時間があり、
それを魔法と呼ぶならば、彼女の言い方は決しておかしなものではない。
contexts.WH: What she chooses to believe weighs little in my thoughts.
contexts.MG:
Maybe it's all girls, not just Shannon, who tend to treat encounters as miracles or coincidences.
For a man like me, an encounter with a girl is 70% hard work to try and make her like you, 20% courage,
and 10% coincidence.
The part that means everything to her...is a much smaller factor in my mind.
...Maybe that way of thinking itself is calculating and typical of men.
But if I said that out loud, it might dissolve all kinds of magic.
To my mind, there were lots of coincidences, compromises, and expended effort on both sides before we gained the relationship we have today.
At the culmination of all that, we get to spend this joyful time together,
and if she wants to call that magic, I've got no objections to her choice of words.
contexts.UP:
Perhaps Shannon isn't alone in wanting to credit an encounter on a miracle, or on chance; it might be a universal thing all girls share.
For a man like me, an encounter with a girl is 70 percent effort to try to please her, and 20 percent raw courage.
And only 10 percent chance.
What she believes to be everything carries little relative weight within me.
...Maybe that way of thinking is in itself calculating and typical of men.
But, were I to express that in words, any kind of magic would be broken.
I do think that to become this close has taken many fortuities, concessions, and great efforts from us both.
We have this private time together now only as the result of all those things put together,
and if she wants to call that "magic", that isn't strange in the slightest.
contexts.note: MG smaller factor and UP relative weight restore comparison between chance/miracle and George combined explanation; neither dismisses everything she believes as personally unimportant.

MG.japanese: 男の僕にとって、女の子との出会いは、気に入られようとする７０％の努力と、２０％の勇気。そして１０％の偶然。彼女が全てだと信じるものは、僕の中では全体を占めるウェートが少ない。…そういう考え方自体が、男性的で打算的なのだろうか。
MG.translation: For a man like me, an encounter with a girl is 70% hard work to try and make her like you, 20% courage, and 10% coincidence. The part that means everything to her...is a much smaller factor in my mind. ...Maybe that way of thinking itself is calculating and typical of men.

UP.japanese: 男の僕にとって、女の子との出会いは、気に入られようとする７０％の努力と、２０％の勇気。そして１０％の偶然。彼女が全てだと信じるものは、僕の中では全体を占めるウェートが少ない。…そういう考え方自体が、男性的で打算的なのだろうか。
UP.translation: For a man like me, an encounter with a girl is 70 percent effort to try to please her, and 20 percent raw courage. And only 10 percent chance. What she believes to be everything carries little relative weight within me. ...Maybe that way of thinking is in itself calculating and typical of men.

findings.sourceReading: The thing Shannon believes accounts for the whole encounter carries only a small proportion of George’s own explanation, immediately after his 70 percent effort, 20 percent courage, and 10 percent chance breakdown.
findings.alternative: “Weighs little” can express importance or causal weighting, and the nearby percentages allow reconstruction. The translation drops her all-encompassing attribution and adds “chooses,” making the line sound more like general dismissal of her beliefs.

findings.description: The passive 強引に抱き寄せられて becomes his forceful embrace “while she dived into my chest,” giving her movement an apparently separate active subject.

その頭を抱え込みながら、二人して水平線を見る。
contexts.japanesePC: 華奢な体が、強引に抱き寄せられて、まるで人形のように僕の胸に飛び込んだ。

彼女の肩を抱き寄せる。

その頭を抱え込みながら、二人して水平線を見る。
contexts.WH: Then I forcefully embraced her entire body while she dived into my chest like a doll.
contexts.MG:
I held her shoulder and drew her close.
When I forcefully pulled her delicate body towards me, she dove into my chest like a doll.
As I held her head in my arms, we both looked at the horizon.
contexts.UP:
I put my arm around her shoulder and held her close.
Her delicate body was pulled irresistibly towards me, and she leapt into my chest like a doll.
As I held her head in my arms, we looked at the horizon together.
contexts.note: MG forceful pulling still followed by she dove. UP restores passive her body was pulled but follows with she leapt, leaving active movement phrasing where source makes doll-like movement consequence of forceful embrace.

MG.translation: I held her shoulder and drew her close. When I forcefully pulled her delicate body towards me, she dove into my chest like a doll. As I held her head in my arms, we both looked at the horizon.

UP.translation: I put my arm around her shoulder and held her close. Her delicate body was pulled irresistibly towards me, and she leapt into my chest like a doll. As I held her head in my arms, we looked at the horizon together.

findings.sourceReading: Her slender body is forcefully drawn close and consequently comes into his chest like a doll.
findings.alternative: The English explicitly retains his forceful embrace and its doll simile, so the physical cause is inferable. Nevertheless “while she dived” suggests concurrent action rather than the result of being pulled.

findings.description: 今は気付けない becomes “then, I hadn’t realized,” moving the expressed temporal perspective into retrospective awareness.

……新しい苦悩の日々の始まりだと、今は気付けない……。

...but at the time, I didn't realize that they'd be the start of a new kind of suffering...

......Those days were like sweetly melting honey,
......but then, I hadn't realized that they were the beginning of days filled with a new kind of suffering......

MG.japanese: そして私は愛を知り、人となることを選ぼうとする。……それは甘く蕩けるような蜜の日々だけれども、……新しい苦悩の日々の始まりだと、今は気付けない……。
MG.translation: So I decided to choose the path of knowing love...and tried to become a person. ...Those days were like sweet honey, ...but at the time, I didn't realize that they'd be the start of a new kind of suffering...

UP.translation: And so I learned of love, and decided to choose to become a person. ......Those days were like sweetly melting honey, ......but then, I hadn't realized that they were the beginning of days filled with a new kind of suffering......

findings.sourceReading: At this moment of choosing love and personhood, Shannon cannot recognize that the honey-sweet days also begin new suffering.
findings.alternative: The entire sequence is introduced as a recollection, and past English can be a natural narrative adjustment. However, the source shifts into the choice’s present and explicitly says “now”; the English replaces that situated ignorance with a later-looking report.

…しかし、この祠に納められている鏡に限っては、むしろそれが何かの神格を感じさせた。

それは古ぼけて曇り、薄汚れた鏡。

findings.sourceReading: For this particular enshrined mirror, the same worn, cloudy, dirty appearance instead conveys some sacred stature.
findings.alternative: “It” in the English may still refer to the old appearance from preceding sentences. Nevertheless the explicit “since ... offered” recasts the reason and drops the contrasting “rather” that applies to that appearance.

findings.description: The repeated temptation to bite the fruit of knowledge becomes “take a bite of true wisdom,” and having already eaten that fruit becomes tasting “that truth.”

知恵の実をかじりなさいと誘惑する。
あるいは、私はもうその実を口にしてしまっているのかもしれない。
contexts.japanesePC:
知恵の実をかじりなさいと誘惑する。
あるいは、私はもうその実を口にしてしまっているのかもしれない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
知恵の実をかじりなさいと誘惑する。
あるいは、私はもうその実を口にしてしまっているのかもしれない。
contexts.WH:
She tempts me to take a bite of true wisdom.

findings.description: A singular trial that is simultaneously small and large becomes “the small and large trials.”

contexts.japanese: これは自分に課す、きっと小さくて大きな試練。
contexts.japanesePC: これは自分に課す、きっと小さくて大きな試練。
contexts.japanesePS3: これは自分に課す、きっと小さくて大きな試練。
contexts.WH: These are surely the small and large trials I must impose on myself.
contexts.MG: This is surely a small...yet large trial I must impose on myself.
contexts.UP: These are surely the small and large trials I must impose on myself.
contexts.note: MG one small yet large trial; UP plural small and large trials.

MG.japanese:
さぁ、勇気を。そして私を家具から解放しよう。
そして新たな苦しみを受け入れることで、人間となろう。
これは自分に課す、きっと小さくて大きな試練。
MG.translation: Come, have courage. I'll free myself from being mere furniture. And by accepting a new kind of suffering, I'll become human. This is surely a small...yet large trial I must impose on myself.

UP.japanese:
さぁ、勇気を。そして私を家具から解放しよう。
そして新たな苦しみを受け入れることで、人間となろう。
これは自分に課す、きっと小さくて大きな試練。
UP.translation:
Come, have courage. I'll free myself from being mere furniture.
And I'll accept my new sufferings, and become human.
These are surely the small and large trials I must impose on myself.

findings.sourceReading: Breaking the mirror is the trial she imposes on herself, surely small yet great.
findings.alternative: The English retains both scale words and self-imposition, and the broader choice involves many difficulties. The demonstrative singular and paradox nevertheless refer to this act, not two classes of trials.

findings.description: MG coordinates past “was ... worried” with present “choose” in the same account of selecting lunch, breaking the intended past-tense narration. UP correctly uses chose.

contexts.japanese:
何て言うのかその、…見栄えを気にしてしまい、
トーストにサラダにコーヒーなんて、キザったらしいメニューにしてしまう。

何て言うのかその、…見栄えを気にしてしまい、
トーストにサラダにコーヒーなんて、キザったらしいメニューにしてしまう。
contexts.MG:
I was...how should I put it...worried about my appearance and choose a menu suited for a snob:
toast, salad and coffee.
contexts.UP:
I was—how should I put it—worried about my appearance,
and chose a menu suited for a snob: toast, salad and coffee.

MG.japanese:
でも、紗音と一緒のバイキングは違う。
好きなものだけみっともなく山盛りにできない。何て言うのかその、…見栄えを気にしてしまい、トーストにサラダにコーヒーなんて、キザったらしいメニューにしてしまう。僕ひとりだったなら、焼きそばやマッシュポテトにグラタン等の油っぽいのを山盛りにしてるところだ。
MG.translation: But with Shannon beside me, this buffet felt different. I couldn't shamefully pile on only the things I liked. I was...how should I put it...worried about my appearance and choose a menu suited for a snob: toast, salad and coffee. If I'd been by myself, I would've made a pile of oily stuff like yakisoba, mashed potatoes, gratin, and so on.

UP.japanese:
でも、紗音と一緒のバイキングは違う。
好きなものだけみっともなく山盛りにできない。何て言うのかその、…見栄えを気にしてしまい、トーストにサラダにコーヒーなんて、キザったらしいメニューにしてしまう。僕ひとりだったなら、焼きそばやマッシュポテトにグラタン等の油っぽいのを山盛りにしてるところだ。

But with Shannon beside me, this buffet felt different.

findings.description: George says they had only exchanged greetings at infrequent family gatherings. MG reduces this to only meeting at those gatherings, dropping the limited interaction that grounds his surprise at their present intimacy. UP explicitly restores only ever exchange greetings.

contexts.japanese:
紗音ちゃんと出会ったのは、昨日今日のことじゃない。
何年も前から面識もある。
でも、年に何度もない親族の会合の席で挨拶をするだけ」

findings.description: Source describes this self-imposed ordeal as small yet large. UP makes these plural small and large trials, replacing one paradoxically assessed act with distinct categories of ordeals. MG preserves a small yet large trial.

contexts.japanese:
さぁ、勇気を。
そして私を家具から解放しよう。
そして新たな苦しみを受け入れることで、人間となろう。
これは自分に課す、きっと小さくて大きな試練。
contexts.japanesePS3:
さぁ、勇気を。

contexts.MG:

I'll free myself from being mere furniture.
And by accepting a new kind of suffering, I'll become human.
This is surely a small...yet large trial I must impose on myself.

findings.description: Source contrasts many days of inner conflict with a recollection far too brief to match them. MG says merely finishing reflections in the blink of an eye, preserving brevity but losing the disproportionate relation. UP restores far too brief to do them justice.

………私は、今日までの葛藤の日々を思い返し、
……それに見合わぬほどわずかな時間で回想を終えて、
……
叩き付けた。

……
叩き付けた。

...
